title: CIA OSI takes UFO research underground, Blue Book as cover

tellings.quote: 1952 the cia's office of scientific intelligence took the real UFO investigations underground they did this while performing a psychological operation the American population in the form of Air Force's Project Blue Book
the long-standing rumors are that this is run by the CIA that in 52 you had public facing UFO UFO research in the form of blue book,
tellings.difference: Framed as long-standing rumor, and credits Battelle and the Atomic Energy Commission.
tellings.link_reason: Both say that in 1952 the CIA ran the real UFO study, with Blue Book as the public-facing front.

as_told.title: CIA running the real UFO study behind Project Blue Book from 1952

tellings.quote: it's now clear in retrospect and I think this is a lot due to Richard Dolan's great research that like you had this cleaving off of the vital study of UFOs the public facing stuff was relegated to project blue book and the air force and then all the private stuff was managed by battel memorial institute
tellings.difference: Says Battelle Memorial Institute ran the private side (Project Stork), credits Richard Dolan, and does not name the CIA OSI.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the 1950s split in which Blue Book was the public face and the real UFO study went private. The story's tellings already involve Battelle.

as_told.title: Project Stork and the Battelle split from Blue Book

tellings.quote: With a small staff, the Air Technical Intelligence Center (ATIC) tried to persuade the public that UFOs were not extraordinary.

Although it had monitored UFO reports for at least three years, CIA reacted to the new rash of sightings by forming a special study group within the Office of Scientific Intelligence (OSI) and the Office of Current Intelligence (OCI) to review the situation.
He also urged that CIA conceal its interest from the media and the public, "in view of their probable alarmist tendencies" to accept such interest as confirming the existence of UFOs.
Air Force and CIA officials agreed that outside knowledge of Agency interest in UFOs would make the problem more serious.

plain: The claim is that in 1952 the CIA moved the real study of UFOs into secret, while the Air Force's public program served as a decoy. Michels tells it himself. He says the CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence took real UFO work underground while running a psychological operation on the public through Project Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. Elsewhere he calls it a long-standing rumor. He also says that, thanks to the researcher Richard Dolan, it is clear the private side was handled by the Battelle Memorial Institute, a research contractor, under something called Project Stork. If true, the public would have spent decades looking at the wrong program. The other source is a history of the CIA's role in studying UFOs, written by Gerald Haines and published by the CIA in 1997. It says that in 1952 the CIA formed "a special study group within the Office of Scientific Intelligence." It says Edward Tauss, reporting for that group, urged "that CIA conceal its interest from the media and the public." It also says the Air Force's intelligence center "tried to persuade the public that UFOs were not extraordinary." That describes a hidden CIA interest next to a public Air Force effort, which is close to what Michels means. Whether Blue Book was a deliberate cover for the hidden work, the history neither says nor rules out.

discussion.by: CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-90
discussion.text: The teller credits Project Blue Book without naming a record. Gerald Haines's history of the CIA's role in the study of UFOs, published by the CIA in 1997, says that in 1952 the CIA formed "a special study group within the Office of Scientific Intelligence (OSI)", that Edward Tauss, reporting for the group, urged "that CIA conceal its interest from the media and the public", and that the Air Force's ATIC "tried to persuade the public that UFOs were not extraordinary"; a hidden CIA interest beside a public Air Force effort is close to what the teller calls taking the research underground. That Blue Book served as a cover or a psychological operation for that hidden work is the teller's step, which the history neither states nor excludes.
